standard_prerequisites.name: Cech complex of the simplicial site
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the horizontal arrows of the double complex (the simplicial cohomology complex).

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of restriction
standard_prerequisites.use: Restriction to C_p is exact, so I_p^bullet represents K_p.

standard_prerequisites.name: Injectivity of restrictions
standard_prerequisites.use: The sheaves I_p^q are injective abelian sheaves on C_p, so column cohomology computes H^q(C_p, K_p).

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1776-1787): for K in D^+(C_total) there is a functorial spectral sequence with E_1^{p,q} = H^q(C_p, K_p), d_1^{p,q} : E_1^{p,q} -> E_1^{p+1,q}, converging to H^{p+q}(C_total, K).

Double complex (proof lines 1789-1797): take a bounded-below complex of injectives I^bullet representing K and form A^{p,q} = Gamma(C_p, I_p^q); the horizontal arrows come from the Cech complex lemma, the vertical ones from the differentials of I^bullet.

Row and column analysis (lines 1799-1810): the rows are exact in positive degrees and evaluate to Gamma(C_total, I^q) in degree 0; since restriction is exact (Lemma lemma-restriction-to-components-site), I_p^bullet represents K_p, and the I_p^q are injective on C_p (Lemma lemma-restriction-injective-to-component-site), so column cohomology computes H^q(C_p, K_p); conclude with the Homology first-quadrant spectral sequence and double-complex resolution lemmas.
proof_roadmap: Represent K by injectives and build the double complex of sections over components.
Check rows exact (simplicial resolution) and columns computing H^q(C_p, K_p).
Apply the standard first-quadrant spectral sequence machinery.
difficulty_reason: Spectral-sequence lemma (statement 1776-1787, proof 1789-1810): the simplicial-site cohomology spectral sequence - the proof constructs the double complex of sections, verifies rows exact (simplicial resolution) and columns computing the E_1-terms (exact restriction plus injectivity preservation, both in-source), and applies the standard Homology machinery; every step is present or named. H2.
